Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

papers.title: Toward planetary microbial systems biology.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms underpin Earth's biosphere, sustaining life, shaping biogeochemical cycles, and maintaining ecosystem stability. In an era of scientific and geopolitical fragmentation, we advocate for a "planetary microbial systems biology" (PMSB) framework to uncover the mechanisms and organizational principles governing Earth's interconnected microbial systems across scales of matter, space, and time and in relation to underlying natural and anthropogenic drivers. PMSB combines molecular and cellular technologies, multi-omics data, artificial intelligence (AI), and integrated transdisciplinary research across ecosystems. By federating open data and combining field observations, experimentation, and modeling, PMSB enables predictive understanding of microbiome dynamics across planetary scales, thus filling a critical knowledge gap in our understanding of the co-evolution of life and the Earth-system.

papers.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images.
papers.abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

papers.title: Short-term memory of past caspase activity biases cell elimination in vivo.
papers.abstract: Apoptosis is triggered by the activation of Caspases leading to irreversible engagement in cell death. However, recent data outline numerous non-apoptotic functions of caspases as well as quite ubiquitous sublethal activation of effector caspases in vivo, opening the question of what drives the bifurcation between cell death and survival. Using quantitative live imaging combined with machine learning and optogenetics in the Drosophila pupal notum (a single-layer epithelium), we reveal the existence of a large heterogeneity of caspase activity thresholds between cells and distinct spatial domains with low or high sensitivity to caspases. We outline the central role of past exposure to sublethal caspase activity, which sensitises cells to apoptosis for several hours and reduces their threshold, and can bias single-cell elimination. Altogether, this work reveals the role of a cell's past history for apoptosis regulation in vivo, which can bias clonal selection and the spatial pattern of cell death.

papers.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational capacity, analogous to scaling up parameters in machine learning models. By contrast, the steering subsystem (hypothalamus, pallidum, and brainstem) scales via diversification of bespoke cell types to encode innate drives and reflexes, functioning as a high-dimensional biological "reward function." This framework explains the divergence in how evolution has influenced these subsystems and offers a unified lens for understanding brain architecture and the etiology of brain disease; furthermore, it may inform model designs for artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Tangermeme: a toolkit for understanding cis-regulatory logic using deep learning models.
papers.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance at predicting diverse genomic modalities, yet their promise for biological discovery lies in how they are used after demonstrating their predictive performance. Here we describe the functionality of tangermeme, a highly optimized toolkit for 'everything-but-the-model' when it comes to genomic deep learning, and demonstrate how tangermeme can be used to distill the learned cis-regulatory patterns from models into human-interpretable insights.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) is foundational to life on Earth, catalyzing carbon dioxide (CO2) fixation to generate biomass. However, Rubisco is a slow and inefficient enzyme that has proven challenging to engineer. We applied the structure-informed machine learning (ML) model ESM-IF1 to identify plausible amino acid sites in the large subunit of Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco to target for directed evolution. ML-assisted library design followed by selection in Rubisco-dependent Escherichia coli identified multiple enriched variants displaying improved catalytic efficiency. Several improved variants carried amino acid changes not found in the evolutionary lineage of plants, despite being assembly competent in plant chloroplasts, demonstrating that ML-assisted protein design can explore functional sequence space beyond what is observed from natural sequence diversity. Most prominently, the T391I substitution improved carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%. Our findings illustrate the utility of ML-assisted evolution for engineering Rubisco with improved carboxylation efficiency and potential for enhancing crop productivity.

papers.title: VenusGenome: Genome-Aware Masked Autoencoding for Microbial Genome Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Genomic-context models have shown that contextualizing protein embeddings can improve predictions of microbial function. We observe that a gene's protein embedding is partially predictable from the embeddings of neighboring genes in the genome, motivating high-ratio masking that requires reconstruction from sparser genomic context. Genomic modeling must also distinguish biological relationships from assembly conventions, since the ordering of separate contigs does not imply adjacency and strand labels depend on the reference orientation. We therefore introduce VenusGenome, a gene-resolution masked autoencoder that combines visible-only encoding with genome-aware attention incorporating contig boundaries, relative strand orientations, and gene positions. We pretrain this model on a curated corpus of over 1.7 million microbial genome assemblies from isolate and metagenomic sources, using frozen protein embeddings as gene-level inputs. Across genome-level phenotype prediction and gene-level tasks, the resulting frozen representations achieve the highest mean performance among the evaluated models on nine of eleven primary metrics. An exploratory gene-input perturbation analysis further links representation sensitivity to experimentally measured fitness defects. Ablations support the contribution of genome-aware attention and show the benefits of masked autoencoding over BERT-style masked modeling, with further gains from higher masking ratios.

papers.title: RNA-SpecFlow: RNA-Conditioned Spectral Flow for Histology Synthesis
papers.abstract: RNA-conditioned histology synthesis models the range of tissue appearances compatible with a transcriptomic representation. We present RNA-SpecFlow, a continuous-latent FlowAR architecture that applies molecular conditioning at adjacent-scale feature transitions. A Biological Latent Adapter maps RNA representations into the generator's condition space. A shared spectral fusion module separates aligned features into complementary low- and high-frequency bands, modulates each band independently with RNA, and combines them through residual fusion. The generator uses five latent grids of sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, with per-scale velocity flow matching and an auxiliary objective for retaining the condition in backbone features. We accompany this architectural specification with an analysis of archived outputs from five TCGA cancer cohorts, including 500 saved real/generated tile pairs. Nuclear analysis yields a concrete measurement finding: increased detection counts can coincide with reduced segmentation agreement. On 12 public images with 303 annotated nuclei, twofold enlargement increases HoVer-Net predictions from 287 to 415 while mean panoptic quality changes from 0.673 to 0.458. Switching analysis pipelines also reverses the direction of real/generated count differences in two cohorts. RNA-SpecFlow provides a design for repeated frequency-specific molecular conditioning, and the accompanying experiments establish the sensitivity of morphology-based evaluation to detector inputs and analysis choices.

papers.title: CAR-macrophage immunotherapy targeting fibroblast-like synoviocytes ameliorates inflammatory and degenerative arthritis
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an inflammatory arthritis, whereas osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease. Despite their distinct etiologies, both are characterized by the pathogenic activation of fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS), which contribute to synovial hyperplasia, persistent inflammation, and cartilage destruction. Accordingly, pathogenic FLS represent an attractive therapeutic target for both RA and OA. Macrophages exhibit remarkable phenotypic plasticity, and interleukin-4 (IL-4) promotes an anti-inflammatory, tissue-reparative M2-like phenotype. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) and nucleolin (NCL) are highly expressed on the surface of pathological FLS while exhibiting limited accessibility in normal tissues. Here, we developed two IL-4-armored, FLS-targeted chimeric antigen receptor macrophage (CAR-M) platforms directed against FAP or NCL, termed CAR-M2-FAP and CAR-M2-NCL, respectively. In vitro, both platforms enhanced FLS phagocytosis and promoted an M2-like transcriptional profile. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed enrichment of phagocytic, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-reparative programs. In a mouse model of RA, both CAR-M2 platforms attenuated arthritis severity, synovial hyperplasia, cartilage loss, and bone erosion. Similarly, in a mouse model of OA, they reduced synovitis, cartilage degeneration, and osteophyte formation. No overt acute toxicity was observed in either RA or OA mice following treatment with CAR-M2-FAP or CAR-M2-NCL. Collectively, the concordant therapeutic effects of CAR-M2-FAP and CAR-M2-NCL across RA and OA models provide preclinical proof of concept for FLS-targeted CAR-M2 as a potential therapeutic strategy for inflammatory and degenerative arthritis.

papers.title: Asymmetric regeneration dynamics in zebrafish pectoral fins
papers.abstract: Appendage amputation in regeneration-capable systems results in the full re-formation of lost tissue and cell populations. Despite an appreciation of this phenomenon in a select number of organisms, there is still much to quantitatively understand about the tissue growth dynamics during limb regeneration. To address these gaps in knowledge, we developed novel methods that enable longitudinal, quantitative imaging of zebrafish pectoral fin regeneration and uncovered a persistent spatial asymmetry in growth dynamics between anterior and posterior regions of the regenerating fin. Spatiotemporally resolved transcriptomics suggests differential anteroposterior regulation of the Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and Wnt signaling pathways in pectoral fins. This asymmetry was also detected using quantitative imaging of biosensors reporting canonical Wnt and Erk pathway activity. In addition to known static spatially asymmetric genes, bulk transcriptomic analysis uncovered a large subset of genes with temporally asymmetric peaks in expression levels between anterior and posterior regions of the fin across regeneration timepoints, suggesting a global differential regulation of the regenerative program. Taken together, our results establish pectoral fins as a platform for quantitative analyses of appendage regeneration, and they identify persistent spatial asymmetries in growth, gene expression, and signaling activity during regeneration.

papers.title: Oyster: A Neural Network for Modeling Genomic Sequences with Exact Position-Specific k-mer Contributions
papers.abstract: Genomics data are sequences, and exploration in these data involves mapping these sequences to function and understanding that mapping. Analogous to a sentence composed of words, a sequence's function is understood through its constituent subsequences, or k-mers. The presence of k-mers, their positions, and their relationships with other k-mers (k-mer associations) all affect sequence function. Understanding the sequence function requires determining the contributions of each of its k-mers and the impacts of their positions and k-mer associations. k-mer associations are inherently combinatorial and may be hierarchical. Although these associations may be impactful for biological phenomena, k-mer associations cannot be understood by humans and severely obfuscate model analyses, yielding generalizations, simplifications, and approximations. Ignoring k-mer associations, however, yields concepts that are human-understandable and exact. To determine whether ignoring k-mer associations is appropriate, models that learn or ignore k-mer associations can be compared. Oyster is a novel NN that learns k-mer composition and k-mer positions while ignoring k-mer associations, the first with these abilities to our knowledge. Oyster is a glass-box model as the exact position-specific contributions of k-mers are directly extracted from the model weights. Oyster is compared with models that consider k-mer associations using two case studies spanning two important genomics topics: protein-DNA interactions and enhancer activity. Across these case studies it was found that while models that consider k-mer associations perform better than Oyster models, the predictions of the Oyster models were in strong agreement, serving as faithful proxies. Human-understandable concepts were extracted from the Oyster models revealing concepts that align with the literature as well as novel ones.

papers.title: Matrix biophysical cues drive transient or prolonged breast cancer dormancy programmes
papers.abstract: Breast cancer metastasis can emerge after disease-free periods through the reawakening of dormant disseminated cancer cells. Despite evidence that the extracellular matrix (ECM) modulates this phenomenon, biophysical cues regulating dormancy fate and therapeutic responses remain poorly understood. Here, we engineered stiffness-matched gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and alginate-based 3D matrices to disentangle matrix stiffness from adhesion and degradability and uncover their contributions to dormancy. Deep learning-based 3D segmentation revealed that adhesive and degradable matrices supported rounded and proliferative tumour masses, whereas inert matrices favoured single cell dormancy. Within inert matrices, stiffness further determined dormancy fate, with soft matrices activating SOX9-associated transient stem-like dormancy, while stiff matrices reduced cell volume, increased intracellular macromolecular crowding of proteins and induced NR2F1-associated prolonged dormancy marked by autophagy and cellular stress. Transiently dormant cells retrieved from soft matrices retained dormancy memory and failed to form tumours in chicken chorioallantoic membranes, demonstrating persistence of matrix-induced states after removal of biophysical cues. Moreover, patient-derived cells in soft inert matrices recapitulated transient dormant states and exhibited therapy resistance. We demonstrate that tuneable biophysical cues shape distinct dormancy states, linking matrix mechanics to dormancy regulation and therapeutic response.

papers.title: Self-Supervised AI Reveals a Hidden Landscape of Prognostic Spatial Patterns in Multiplex Immunofluorescence Images
papers.abstract: Modern spatial proteomic methods, such as multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) imaging, offer a data-rich view of spatial biology in intact tissues. However, interpreting its complexity is a major bottleneck, limiting its potential for biological discovery and clinical translation. Current computational methods often rely on segmentation-based approaches that discard crucial morphological information and are limited to testing pre-defined hypotheses. Here, we introduce a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework that enables hypothesis-agnostic, context-aware discovery of biomarkers directly from mIF images. Our approach extracts rich feature representations that capture holistic architectural patterns, which integrate cellular morphology, marker interactions, and microenvironmental context without human supervision. Applying this framework to over 7,000 mIF tissue images from over 1,800 patients in two distinct cancer types, we demonstrate superior prognostic performance over conventional segmentation analyses. The method autonomously identified previously unknown and potentially clinically actionable biological patterns. In lung adenocarcinoma, these include a Ki67-mediated immune evasion phenotype, a subcellular pattern of GLB1 expression which aligns with low-grade EGFR-driven tumours, and distinct modes of tumour-immune interaction in PD-L1+ patients. We also find a regulatory T-cell-mediated immunosupressive environment promoting tumour budding in colorectal carcinoma. Our work establishes SSL as a powerful, scalable, and unbiased platform to decode tissue ecosystems while being fully explainable without pre-defined hypotheses. This paradigm shift transforms high-plex imaging from a hypothesis-testing tool into a hypothesis-generating engine that can accelerate the discovery of next-generation spatial biomarkers.

papers.title: Serum nutritional-metabolic recovery during tuberculosis treatment across BMI-defined undernutrition strata: A longitudinal proteomic reanalysis
papers.abstract: Background Tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, and undernutrition is a major modifiable risk factor. Serum proteomics can capture systemic host recovery during therapy, but whether baseline BMI-defined undernutrition alters this trajectory is unclear. Methods We reanalysed processed longitudinal tandem-mass-tag serum proteomics from 30 adults with pulmonary tuberculosis and durable cure sampled at baseline and weeks 8, 17, 26 and 52. Thirteen participants had baseline BMI =18.5 kg/m2. Protein-level analyses evaluated baseline differences and week-specific within-participant change; module and recovery-axis models evaluated BMI-by-time interactions, with random-intercept mixed models added as a repeated-measures sensitivity analysis. Three complementary treatment-responsive modules were integrated into an exploratory, nonredundant 36-protein nutritional-metabolic summary axis. Results The reconstructed dataset contained 1,923 quantified features across 150 participant-visits. Inflammatory/acute-phase and metal-handling/nutritional-immunity module scores declined during follow-up, whereas lipid/apolipoprotein-transport, nutritional-carrier and endocrine-immunometabolic scores increased. In the primary week-specific paired-change analyses, no protein-level between-BMI difference in longitudinal change survived false-discovery-rate correction; no curated-module BMI-by-time interaction survived correction. The 36-protein summary axis increased in both BMI strata from week 17 onward. In a random-intercept model without interaction, the BMI =18.5 kg/m2 comparison stratum, although the confidence interval included zero (difference -1.34, 95% CI -2.76 to 0.08; p = .064). Categorical and continuous BMI-by-time interaction tests did not detect differential axis trajectories. Conclusions Tuberculosis treatment was accompanied by broad longitudinal remodelling of circulating inflammatory and nutritional-metabolic protein systems. An exploratory 36-protein summary axis increased in both baseline BMI strata, while formal interaction tests did not detect BMI-dependent trajectories and remained too imprecise to establish equivalence. BMI should be regarded as an anthropometric proxy rather than a comprehensive measure of nutritional state. The defined axis provides a framework for prospective validation alongside direct measures of body composition, micronutrients, treatment exposure and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from human kidney tissue. Kidzoi accurately predicts cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility and improves regulatory variant effect prediction in proximal tubule cells by up to 23% in terms of AUROC over existing models. Furthermore, Kidzoi effectively prioritizes genome-wide association study (GWAS) fine-mapped causal variants associated with kidney function (estimated glomerular filtration rate based on both creatinine and cystatin C; eGFRcr-cys) while resolving their cell-type specificity. Systematic ablation of flanking sequence indicates that a local context of 32-64kbp, representing only 6-12% of the full model input, captures most of the information needed for variant effect prediction. Finally, we show that a multi-task model achieves comparable performance to single-task models at a substantially reduced computational cost.

papers.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
papers.abstract: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of positions are simultaneously accessible on individual molecules. Then, we train ChAI-Net, a neural network that predicts these locus-specific chromatin co-accessibility maps from the underlying DNA sequence. Through model interpretation and in silico experiments, we show that ChAI-Net learns unique combinations of sequence motifs underlying co-accessibility within enhancers, promoters, and CTCF-bound sites. Many of these motifs are missed when modeling average accessibility, suggesting a specific role in coordinated binding. ChAI-Net's regulatory grammar also highlights the importance of TF motif orientation, spacing, positioning, and co-occurrence in driving co-accessibility. Thus, our framework for extracting regulatory rules from footprinting data expands understanding of TF cooperativity, while laying the groundwork to elucidate how these rules vary across cellular contexts as single-molecule genomics is deployed at scale.

papers.title: Differentiable Spin-Center Diffusion Model Enables DEER-Guided Generative Pipeline of Weighted Protein Ensembles
papers.abstract: Biological function entails the interconversion of a protein between distinct conformations, an equilibrium modulated by ligands and other physicochemical conditions. Double electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy captures these ensembles as distance distributions, P(r), between spin label pairs. However, the width of P(r) convolves protein conformational heterogeneity with the rotameric flexibility of the label. Because current spin label models overestimate this contribution, translating P(r) into ensembles has remained indirect and predominantly qualitative. Here, we developed spin-center (SC) diffusion, a differentiable model of the spin label with a tunable spin label rotameric width. Coupled to a frozen Boltz-2 structure generator, SC diffusion enables the entire experimental P(r) to guide ensemble generation at inference time. We demonstrate the robustness of this pipeline on synthetic P(r) of known composition, recovering the ensemble populations, including both components of a bimodal profile. Guided by experimental P(r) measured under different biochemical conditions, ensembles of the transporters PfMATE, LmrP, MhsT and P-glycoprotein were modeled and free energy differences derived from the ensembles in a condition-dependent manner. By embedding a differentiable label model in structure generation, our approach interprets DEER distributions as weighted conformational ensembles, adding a missing thermodynamic grounding to generative protein structure prediction methods.

papers.title: A collaborative submission model for building high-quality data resources at scale through partnership: lessons from single-cell genomics
papers.abstract: Community data resources that aggregate datasets across studies are critical infrastructure for modern biomedical research, accelerating discovery, and rapidly-advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) models place ever-greater demand on large, well-described data corpora. However, building these resources involves a fundamental tension: comprehensive metadata is imperative for reuse, yet capturing this information systematically requires substantial effort that limits growth. We detail how CZ CELLxGENE Discover has used a collaborative submission model, whereby data contributors partner with dedicated resource curators, to become a large, widely used single-cell genomics resource for diverse analytical applications including AI model development and integrative analysis. This partnership leverages contributors' intimate study knowledge and curators' focus on data reuse and expertise in standardization to improve data quality, metadata accuracy, and richness. This is achieved by motivating researcher participation through tangible benefits while minimizing submission burden. We contrast this collaborative model with contributor-driven and resource-driven approaches, highlighting tradeoffs in scalability, consistency across submissions, and quality assurance. The principles and practices we describe provide a framework for building high-quality community data resources across diverse biological data types.

papers.title: SMARCA4 MUTATIONS PROMOTE CHEMOTHERAPY RESISTANCE IN T-ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA THROUGH ALTERED CHROMATIN REMODELING AT AP1-ASSOCIATED REGULATORY REGIONS
papers.abstract: Chromatin remodelers play a critical role in orchestrating chemotherapy responses in cancer cells. Components of the SWI/SNF complex are frequently mutated across cancer types, with the ATPase subunit SMARCA4 among the most commonly altered. In T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), however, SMARCA4 mutations are rare at diagnosis but enriched in relapse samples, suggesting a potential role in therapy resistance. Using isogenic T-ALL cell lines with or without SMARCA4 mutations, we show that mutant SMARCA4 confers resistance to a broad range of chemotherapeutic agents. By combining ATAC-seq and RNA-seq, we demonstrate that SMARCA4-mutant cells display an attenuated transcriptional response to chemotherapy accompanied by impaired remodeling of AP-1-associated regulatory regions linked to stress response. These cells downregulate stress-related genes while maintaining expression programs associated with cellular fitness. Pharmacological inhibition of AP-1 phenocopies this response, further supporting a functional link between SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling at AP-1-associated regulatory regions, AP-1 activity, and chemotherapy sensitivity. Together, our findings indicate that SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling of these regions contributes to an effective chemotherapy-induced stress response, and that its failure provides T-ALL cells with a survival

papers.title: BioResearchBench: 50 Long Horizon Biological Research Tasks
papers.abstract: AI models are used in biology research to study disease mechanisms, discover potential treatments, analyze experimental data, troubleshoot problems, and plan next steps. Useful assistance depends on working with data in various scientific formats, interpreting results, and deciding what to test next. We present BioResearchBench, a benchmark of 50 research questions developed by PhD biologists drawing on their deep research expertise to reflect realistic problems encountered in their fields. Questions were refined through expert review and iterative model testing. The collection spans 10 diverse biology subdomains and includes sequencing data, proteomic measurements, microscopy images, assay readouts, and clinical datasets. We compared recorded outcomes and examined model responses in depth across the 50 tasks on OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Meta Muse Wonder, and SpaceXSI Grok 4.7. Success across our benchmark was 18% for Claude Opus 5.5, 13% for Gemini 4 Argon, 11% for Meta Muse Wonder, 4% for GPT-6 Astra, and 4% for Grok 4.7. These results describe a deliberately challenging collection selected through expert review and model testing. Despite low whole task success, the selected responses met most rubric requirements on average: the average fraction of criteria missed ranged from 18% to 32% across models. Across models, the proportion of eligible tasks with at least one category failure was highest in computation and data handling (66.9% failure), followed by uncertainty and identification (55.3% failure), reporting and completeness (54.7% failure), biological interpretation (39.0% failure), controls and causal claims (37.2% failure), and choosing the next experiment or decision (31.0% failure). Gemini 4 Argon had the highest proportion of reviewed tasks without a recorded category failure in computation and data handling (45% success) and biological interpretation (69% success). Claude Opus 5.5 led in controls and causal claims (72% success) and choosing the next experiment or decision (75% success). GPT-6 Astra led in uncertainty and identification (56% success) which included judging the precision of estimates and recognizing when measurements could not distinguish between biological explanations. GPT-6 Astra and Meta Muse Wonder tied for the highest proportion of answers with no recorded omissions or reporting failures (51% success). Five case studies presented here show how top AI models can perform many analytical steps correctly yet misinterpret what results signify. For example, some answers described cells as fully recovered when oxygen consumption improved even though mitochondrial membrane potential and cell number remained below control levels. These model answers therefore overstated the extent of cell recovery. Other answers incorrectly called a protein a direct microRNA target, although the experiment had not tested whether the microRNA acted directly on its mRNA or affected it through another process.
